rendered: The document does not say that S. aureus had the lowest limit of detection, and it gives no LOD for S. aureus at all, so it cannot explain why. The only LOD values it reports are for P. aeruginosa and L. monocytogenes. The text states that CD consistently achieved lower limit of detection[1] than UV–vis. For P. aeruginosa, the text reports P. aeruginosa had an LOD of OD600 =0.0034 (CD,[2] For L. monocytogenes, it reports presented an LOD of 0.0123 (CD, Fig. S17c)[3]. S. aureus is mentioned only in the concentration-dependent LDA results, where the text says that only partial discrimination[4] was achieved for S. typhimurium and S. aureus[5]. The only S. aureus-specific signal reading in the figures is a model reading of the panel d caption, which says that In panel d, S.aureus gives ΔCD of about -14 mdeg, the smallest magnitude.[6] That is a signal magnitude, not an LOD, and the document does not link it to detection limits.
